outputs.L1: The invention relates to a puncturing system comprising an outer tubular body configured to remain in a body part of a living being. The puncturing system is characterized in that it comprises at least one inner tubular body and a puncturing needle, wherein the inner tubular body is guided through a working lumen of the outer tubular body and is longitudinally displaceable relative to the outer tubular body, and wherein the puncturing needle is guided through a puncture lumen of the inner tubular body and the inner tubular body is longitudinally displaceable relative to the puncturing needle. After a body part has been punctured by means of a puncturing section of the puncturing needle protruding from a patient-side end of the puncturing system, the inner tubular body can be advanced from the patient-side end of the catheter at least partially out of the outer tubular body, thereby being configured to receive, at least partially within the puncture lumen of the inner tubular body, the puncturing section of the puncturing needle protruding from the patient-side end of the catheter.
outputs.L2: The invention concerns a puncture system that includes an outer tube intended to stay positioned within a body part of a living organism. The system is distinguished by the presence of at least one internal tube and a puncture needle. The internal tube extends through a working lumen of the outer tube and is movable in the lengthwise direction relative to the outer tube. The puncture needle passes through a puncture lumen of the internal tube, and the internal tube is likewise longitudinally movable relative to the puncture needle. After the body part has been pierced by a puncturing portion of the needle projecting from the patient-facing end of the puncture system, the internal tube can be advanced from the patient-side end of the catheter so that it emerges at least partly from the outer tube. In this position, the internal tube is configured to receive, at least partially within its puncture lumen, the puncturing portion of the needle that extends beyond the patient-side end of the catheter.
outputs.L3:
The invention relates to a puncturing system for use in a body part of a living being. The system comprises an outer tubular body that is configured and dimensioned to remain, at least temporarily, in the body part after placement. This outer tubular body may serve as an access element or guide structure for introducing or manipulating further instruments within the body.

The puncturing system further includes at least one inner tubular body and a puncturing needle. The inner tubular body is arranged so that it can be introduced through a working lumen of the outer tubular body. Within this working lumen, the inner tubular body is guided in a manner that permits longitudinal movement relative to the outer tubular body. As a result, the inner tubular body can be advanced or retracted through the outer tubular body as required during the puncturing procedure.

The puncturing needle is guided through a puncture lumen formed in the inner tubular body. The arrangement is such that the inner tubular body is also longitudinally movable relative to the puncturing needle. This allows the puncturing needle and the inner tubular body to be positioned with respect to one another in different operative states, for example during insertion, puncturing, and subsequent protection or covering of the needle.

During use, the puncturing needle may initially project beyond the distal end of the inner tubular body so that its puncturing section can penetrate the target body part. After the puncture has been made, the inner tubular body can be advanced in the distal direction relative to the puncturing needle. By doing so, the inner tubular body at least partially receives or accommodates the protruding puncturing section of the needle within its puncture lumen. In this position, the sharp or traumatic portion of the puncturing needle is at least partly shielded by the inner tubular body, which can reduce the risk of unintended injury to surrounding tissue and facilitate safer handling of the puncturing system.
outputs.L4:
The present invention relates to a puncturing and catheter placement system for safely accessing a target site within a living body and for placing a catheter or similar tubular member at the accessed site. The system is particularly useful in medical procedures in which a puncturing needle must be introduced through tissue and then withdrawn or shielded after access has been obtained, while maintaining the position of an outer tubular member in the body.

The system includes an outer tubular body, an inner tubular body, and a puncturing needle. The outer tubular body is configured to be inserted into the living body and to remain in position after puncture so that it can function as a catheter, sheath, guide, or access passage. The inner tubular body is arranged inside the outer tubular body and is movable in the longitudinal direction relative to the outer tubular body. The puncturing needle is inserted through the lumen of the inner tubular body and is guided by the inner tubular body during advancement toward the puncture site.

During use, the puncturing needle is positioned so that its sharp distal tip projects beyond the distal end of the inner tubular body, allowing the needle to puncture skin, tissue, a vessel wall, an organ wall, or another biological structure. The outer tubular body is advanced together with or after the needle so that the distal portion of the outer tubular body reaches the desired placement location. In this state, the outer tubular body can be held in place to maintain access to the interior of the target site.

After the puncture has been made, the inner tubular body is advanced in the distal direction relative to the puncturing needle and/or the outer tubular body. By this movement, the distal end portion of the inner tubular body moves toward the protruding needle tip and at least partially covers the needle tip within the lumen of the inner tubular body. In this covered state, the sharp tip of the puncturing needle is no longer fully exposed outside the inner tubular body. As a result, the likelihood of unintended injury to surrounding tissue, damage to the outer tubular body, accidental needle-stick injury, or other hazardous contact with the exposed needle tip is reduced.

The outer tubular body may remain positioned in the living body while the needle tip is covered by the inner tubular body. This allows the operator to improve safety without losing access to the puncture site. The puncturing needle may then be withdrawn through the inner tubular body, or the inner tubular body and puncturing needle may be removed together, while the outer tubular body remains indwelling as a catheter or access sheath. Alternatively, the inner tubular body may remain temporarily in place as a protective guide during subsequent manipulation.

By providing a longitudinally movable inner tubular body that can be advanced to cover the distal tip of the puncturing needle after puncture, the invention improves procedural safety and handling. The system enables reliable puncture and placement while reducing the risk associated with an exposed sharp needle tip. It also permits the outer tubular body to remain accurately positioned in the body, thereby supporting stable catheter placement and reducing the need for repeated puncture attempts.

**The Power of “The”**

“The” is one of the smallest and most common words in the English language, yet it plays an important role in communication. It is called a definite article, which means it points to something specific. For example, when we say “a book,” we could mean any book. But when we say “the book,” we are talking about a particular book that both the speaker and listener understand.

Although “the” is short, it helps make sentences clear and precise. It tells us that something is known, unique, or already mentioned. We use it in phrases like “the sun,” “the world,” “the best choice,” and “the answer.” Without this simple word, English would often feel less natural and more confusing.

“The” also appears in many titles, names, and expressions. It can give importance to a subject, making it sound specific or meaningful. For example, “the moment,” “the truth,” or “the beginning” all feel stronger because of this small word.

In everyday language, “the” may seem ordinary, but it is essential. It connects ideas, creates clarity, and helps people understand exactly what is being discussed. Sometimes, the smallest words have the greatest impact.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style independent claim for a medical puncturing system with an outer catheter tube, a movable inner tube, and a puncturing needle, where the inner tube can advance to cover the needle tip after puncture.
counterfactuals.output:
1. A medical puncturing system comprising:

an outer catheter tube having a proximal end, a distal end, and a lumen extending therebetween;

an inner tube disposed at least partially within the lumen of the outer catheter tube and movable relative to the outer catheter tube between a retracted position and an advanced position; and

a puncturing needle extending through at least a portion of the inner tube and having a distal needle tip configured to protrude distally beyond the distal end of the outer catheter tube during puncturing of tissue,

wherein, in the retracted position of the inner tube, the distal needle tip is exposed to permit puncturing,

and wherein, after puncturing, the inner tube is advanceable distally relative to the puncturing needle such that a distal end portion of the inner tube covers the distal needle tip, thereby shielding the distal needle tip within the inner tube.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a formal patent abstract/claim for a catheter puncturing system in which an inner cannula slides relative to both an outer cannula and a needle and can receive the protruding puncture section after insertion.
counterfactuals.output:
**Abstract**

A catheter puncturing system includes an outer cannula, a needle disposed at least partially within the outer cannula and having a distal puncture section configured to penetrate tissue, and an inner cannula slidably arranged relative to both the outer cannula and the needle. The inner cannula is movable between a retracted position, in which the puncture section of the needle protrudes distally for insertion of the catheter puncturing system, and an advanced receiving position, in which the inner cannula receives or surrounds at least a portion of the protruding puncture section after insertion. The arrangement permits controlled exposure of the puncture section during puncture and shielding or containment of the puncture section following placement, thereby reducing unintended tissue trauma and facilitating safe positioning of the catheter assembly.

**Claim**

1. A catheter puncturing system comprising:  
   an outer cannula having a proximal end, a distal end, and a lumen extending therebetween;  
   a needle disposed at least partially within the lumen of the outer cannula, the needle including a distal puncture section configured to protrude beyond the distal end of the outer cannula during insertion; and  
   an inner cannula disposed at least partially within the outer cannula and configured to slide relative to both the outer cannula and the needle,  
   wherein the inner cannula is movable from a first position, in which the distal puncture section of the needle is exposed for puncturing tissue, to a second position, in which the inner cannula receives at least a portion of the distal puncture section after insertion of the catheter puncturing system.

2. The catheter puncturing system of claim 1, wherein the inner cannula defines a distal receiving lumen sized to accommodate the distal puncture section of the needle.

3. The catheter puncturing system of claim 1, wherein the inner cannula is advanced distally relative to the needle to receive the distal puncture section.

4. The catheter puncturing system of claim 1, wherein the needle is retractable relative to the inner cannula after the distal puncture section has been received by the inner cannula.

5. The catheter puncturing system of claim 1, wherein movement of the inner cannula to the second position shields a sharpened tip of the distal puncture section.

6. The catheter puncturing system of claim 1, further comprising an actuator operatively coupled to the inner cannula and configured to move the inner cannula relative to the outer cannula and the needle.

7. The catheter puncturing system of claim 6, wherein the actuator is disposed at a proximal hub of the catheter puncturing system.

8. The catheter puncturing system of claim 1, wherein the outer cannula is configured to remain positioned in a body lumen after withdrawal of the needle.

9. The catheter puncturing system of claim 1, wherein the inner cannula is coaxially arranged between the outer cannula and the needle.

10. The catheter puncturing system of claim 1, wherein the inner cannula, in the second position, reduces exposure of the distal puncture section beyond the distal end of the outer cannula.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3
